words: Small glass ball used in traditional games
Send a marble toward a target
Hue, such as red or blue
Move by turning over and over on the ground
Body part with fingers and a thumb

answerNotes.MARBLE: A playing marble is a small hard ball, often glass. The name here does not refer to the stone used for countertops.
answerNotes.GLASS: Glass is usually transparent but can also be colored. A glass is a drinking vessel, while glass without an article can name the material.
answerNotes.CIRCLE: A circle is a round line or shape. In a marble game, a drawn circle can mark the playing area.
answerNotes.GAME: Game names the organized activity or contest. Equipment such as a bat or board is used in the game but is not the game itself.
answerNotes.BAG: A bag is a flexible carrying container. A pocket is generally a smaller compartment attached to clothing or another bag.
answerNotes.COLOR: Color names such as red, blue, and yellow describe appearance. They can help with a flower scene without requiring botanical vocabulary.
answerNotes.AIM: Aim means direct something toward a target. It is an action, unlike the target or the object being thrown.
answerNotes.HAND: Hand can name a body part or a clock pointer. A clock's minute hand makes a full turn each hour.

words: Soft white stick for writing on a board

Send through the air by hand

answerNotes.HOPSCOTCH: Hopscotch uses a numbered ground pattern and a small marker. Local versions differ, so the puzzle focuses on its familiar equipment and actions.
answerNotes.CHALK: Chalk leaves a powdery mark that can be wiped away. It is useful on a board or pavement but does not behave like permanent ink.
answerNotes.NUMBER: A number can count an amount or identify something. A telephone number identifies a connection rather than measuring its size.
answerNotes.HOP: Hopping uses a springing jump. In hopscotch, the grid determines which spaces are used for one foot or two.
answerNotes.FOOT: A foot is a body part and also a unit of length. A shoe clue points to the body meaning rather than twelve inches.
answerNotes.STONE: Stone is a piece of natural rock. A slab is a relatively flat piece, while gravel consists of many smaller pieces.
answerNotes.LINE: Line can mean a row, a drawn mark, or a fishing cord. The clue's action helps distinguish those meanings.
answerNotes.GAME: Game names the organized activity or contest. Equipment such as a bat or board is used in the game but is not the game itself.

words: Small metal game pieces picked up after bouncing a ball
Round toy that can roll or bounce
Flexible material used in boots and tires
Grasping part at the end of an arm
Take hold of a thrown ball
Material such as iron or copper

answerNotes.JACKS: Jacks are small game pieces, often metal. Players pick them up between bounces of a ball, with the required count increasing by round.
answerNotes.BOUNCE: A bounce is the return movement after striking a surface. A rubber ball's springiness lets it rise after hitting the floor.
answerNotes.BALL: A ball is usually round in games such as baseball. American football uses a different, elongated shape.
answerNotes.RUBBER: Rubber bends and springs back. That makes it useful for balls and tires as well as waterproof footwear.
answerNotes.PICK: Pick can mean choose or pluck. In a harvest setting, it usually means gathering something from the plant.
answerNotes.HAND: Hand can name a body part or a clock pointer. A clock's minute hand makes a full turn each hour.
answerNotes.GAME: Game names the organized activity or contest. Equipment such as a bat or board is used in the game but is not the game itself.
answerNotes.METAL: Metal names a family of materials including iron, copper, and aluminum. The word does not identify which metal a particular tool contains.

words: Toy that spins on a point

answerNotes.TOP: A toy top spins on a point. Top can also mean the highest part of an object, so the action in the clue matters.
answerNotes.SPIN: Spin means rotate around a center. A top stays upright while turning quickly, then wobbles as it slows.
answerNotes.STRING: String is a thin cord used for tying or flying a kite. A kite's string connects the flying frame to the person holding it.
answerNotes.WOOD: Wood comes from trees and has a grain. Following that grain when sanding usually leaves a smoother surface.
answerNotes.POINT: Point names a tapered end. A sharpened pencil needs a usable point, while a worn one makes a broader mark.
answerNotes.WIND: Wind has two pronunciations and meanings: moving air, or turning something around a center. A yarn ball or clock uses the turning action.
answerNotes.TOY: A toy is made for play. A miniature model can be a toy, a hobby project, or a display depending on its use.
answerNotes.COLOR: Color names such as red, blue, and yellow describe appearance. They can help with a flower scene without requiring botanical vocabulary.

answerNotes.BLANKET: A blanket is a covering used for warmth. A quilt usually has several layers held together with stitching.
answerNotes.CUP: Cup can name a drinking vessel or a measuring amount. A recipe's measured cup is not simply any small mug.
answerNotes.PLATE: A plate is flatter than a bowl. Its broad surface is useful for separate portions of a meal.
answerNotes.BASKET: A basket is made by weaving flexible material. Its open structure and carrying handle make it useful for collecting garden produce.
answerNotes.TOY: A toy is made for play. A miniature model can be a toy, a hobby project, or a display depending on its use.
answerNotes.TABLE: A table provides a raised flat surface. Chairs are the separate furniture used to sit beside it.
